clue.text: Sordid details

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means mean, dishonourable or sordid
the inside information or full facts about something, as in 'give me the details'

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: an adjective for base or dishonourable conduct and an informal noun for the inside story.

clue.text: See former pupil do his duty

parts.note: OB is short for old boy, a former pupil of a school
to serve is to carry out one's duty, as a soldier or servant does

explanation.surface: A school old boy is told to carry out his obligations.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe something is to see or notice it; a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Close match may have been so tense

definitions.text: Close match may have been so
definitions.meaning: a closely fought game may end level, with neither side winning
... describes a face or nerves pulled tight with strain

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers a game ending level and a strained, haggard look under tension.

clue.text: Expressing a choice of alternatives — sun and rain, say

indicators.note: say tells us the word is spoken, so we want something that sounds like it

parts.note: sunshine and rain are both kinds of weather

explanation.surface: A forecaster weighing up between a sunny and a rainy outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like it just introduces examples of weather, but it also asks for a word pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction introduces alternatives, as in 'whether you like it or not', so it expresses a choice.

clue.text: Old bean is so mean — that's about right

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: mean in the sense of miserly is stingy

explanation.surface: Someone calls a friend 'old bean' and accuses them of being tight-fisted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old bean' reads as a jocular British form of address, but it is a literal vegetable: an old runner bean gets tough and fibrous.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageing beans develop tough fibres along their pods, so an old bean is fibrous in exactly this way.

clue.text: Yank about to dispose of pipes

indicators.note: about here means going round, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: to yank something is to tug it sharply
to bin something is to throw it away

explanation.surface: An American is about to throw away some plumbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American person, but it is a verb meaning pull sharply.
explanation.definitionFit: Tubing is lengths of tube collectively, which is to say pipes.

clue.text: Preparation of ricin isn't essential

indicators.note: a preparation makes something up from ingredients, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that making the poison ricin is not fundamental.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intrinsic belongs to a thing's basic nature, so it is essential to it.

clue.text: Abandon the sick in Kentish Town, being material

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: Gillingham is a town in the English county of Kent
people who are ill, the ill

explanation.surface: Leaving invalids behind in a district of north London called Kentish Town.
explanation.walkthrough: Kentish Town is a real part of London, but here it means any town in Kent, the county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Gingham is a checked cotton fabric, so it is a type of material.

clue.text: Given large drink and a spliff, journalist can twist your arm?

parts.note: a double is a double measure of spirits
a joint is a cannabis cigarette, also called a spliff
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A heavy night of drink and drugs leaves a reporter able to persuade anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twist your arm' usually means pressure someone; here it is literal, about flexible joints.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with unusually flexible joints can bend limbs, such as an arm, further than normal.

clue.text: A former country detailed its location

indicators.note: de-tailed, with its tail or last letter cut off

parts.note: Siam was the former name of Thailand

explanation.surface: A country that no longer exists had its position recorded precisely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' reads as 'described closely' but means losing the last letter. 'its' refers back to the former country.
explanation.definitionFit: Siam, now Thailand, lies in this continent, which is therefore where it is located.

clue.text: Old World movement offered a new religious text — a price too high to pay

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife
an orbit is the path a world or planet follows around a star
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: A new scripture offered by an Old World movement comes at a steep cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old World' reads as a phrase meaning Europe and Asia, but 'Old' and 'World movement' are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Exorbitant prices are excessive, far beyond what is reasonable to pay.

clue.text: Possible headline describing the day Joan of Arc had her chips?

definitions.text: Possible headline describing the day Joan of Arc had her chips?

parts.words: Possible headline describing the day Joan of Arc had her chips?
parts.note: Joan of Arc was a Frenchwoman burnt at the stake; 'had her chips' means met her end, and the whole also names a fried potato dish

explanation.definitionFit: The dish is thin fried potato strips, which British speakers call chips.

clue.text: An unsavoury incident?

parts.note: unsavoury normally means disreputable, but read literally a fight with sweet buns rather than savoury food is a sweet, not savoury, clash

explanation.definitionFit: A bun fight is a British informal term for a squabble or a tea party, here read as a scuffle with buns.

clue.text: A card game, of course

definitions.meaning: a gambling card game in which players lay cards to match horses on the table
a racecourse: ... in Suffolk is the home of British horse racing

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a card game and to a famous English racecourse.

clue.text: Tongue which may twist

indicators.note: turning the word round end to end leaves it unchanged, so it may be twisted

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A description of a language that can be twisted round.
explanation.definitionFit: Malayalam is the language of Kerala in southern India; tongue means language.

clue.text: Into which Xhosa marquetry has been laden, roughly speaking

indicators.note: the answer has gone into these words, sitting within them

explanation.surface: Inlaid woodwork made by the Xhosa people has been loaded onto something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'been', roughly speaking, sounds like 'bin', giving the name of the al-Qaeda leader Osama bin Laden; 'which' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The full name Osama bin Laden is suggested by the first name followed by 'been laden' said loosely.

clue.text: In discussion, head for row

indicators.note: in discussion means spoken out, so the word is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: the skull is the bony part of the head

explanation.surface: Talking things over, the leader goes for a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like an argument (to rhyme with 'cow'), but it means propel a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To scull is to propel a boat with oars, so it means to row.

clue.text: Adversary caught heading the wrong way, 'e's locked up with set of keys

indicators.note: locked up means imprisoned, so one piece is placed inside another
travelling in the wrong direction, so these letters are written back to front

parts.note: a rival is an opponent or adversary
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
'e is a dropped-aitch he, shown as the letter E

explanation.surface: An enemy captured going the wrong way has been jailed along with some keys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading the wrong way' turns RIVAL plus C to give CLAVIR, and 'locked up' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A clavier is a keyboard instrument, a set of keys like a harpsichord or piano keyboard.

clue.text: Giving flower to male is foolishness

parts.note: the poppy is a red flower
a cock is a male bird

explanation.surface: Presenting a bloom to a man is a silly idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Poppycock is informal for nonsense, which is foolishness.

clue.text: Finger the dog

definitions.meaning: something that indicates, as a finger points to an object
a breed of gun dog that stands still with its nose aimed at game

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an indicating finger or stick and a breed of gun dog.

clue.text: Wow! Lovely example of moulding

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like wow
nice means pleasant or lovely

explanation.surface: An admiring exclamation at a fine piece of decorative plasterwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornice is an ornamental moulding running along the top of a wall, so it is one kind of moulding.

clue.text: Tuareg's forbidding home leave

definitions.meaning: the Tuareg are nomads of the Sahara, a harsh, dry wilderness
to abandon, as a soldier going absent without leave

explanation.definitionFit: The noun is the arid land of the Sahara and the verb means abandon or leave.

clue.text: One distanced from the mistreatment of a friendly woodland resident

indicators.note: mistreatment means handling roughly, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone banished from a gentle forest creature after harming it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One distanced from' means the letter I comes out of the letters of A FRIENDLY before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The lady fern is a delicate fern that grows in woods, so it lives there.

clue.text: Weak, though employed?

definitions.meaning: weak, especially through age or illness
read as two words, being in a firm means having a job

explanation.definitionFit: The word means feeble, and split in two it describes someone working for a company.

clue.text: See 12
Grabbing uniform, lifted out of place where shot, perhaps

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing hold of, so one piece holds the other within it
out of place means disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: even means uniform or regular

explanation.surface: A soldier's kit is snatched and stolen from the spot where someone was gunned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' looks like 'stolen' but is anagram fodder; 'out of place' turns it into FIELDT. 'shot' is the shot put, an athletics throwing event, not gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: The shot put is an athletics contest held in the field rather than on the track, so it is one example.

clue.text: Bird losing way going west is a wader

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left, backwards

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A bird that has lost its route and heads west turns out to be a wading bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' is the word itself: taking out RD leaves BI, which 'going west' turns to IB.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged bird that wades in shallows, so it is a wader.

clue.text: Make to bury male — or do otherwise?

indicators.note: to bury is to put something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to make something is to create it

explanation.surface: A question of whether to inter a man or take another course.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'bury': the alternative to burying a body is to burn it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather than burying the dead, one may burn them to ashes, the other way to deal with a body.

clue.text: Tied up with financial administration on the phone?

indicators.note: heard down a phone line, so we want a word that is spoken alike

parts.note: a trust is an arrangement for administering money or property on someone's behalf

explanation.surface: Someone tied up with money matters while making a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: Trussed means bound tightly, as poultry is tied before roasting.
